tools.fields: [operation?:"definition"|"typeDefinition"|"implementation", path*, symbolName*, contextLines?, limit?, line?, occurrence?, …] | [operation?:"definition"|"typeDefinition"|"implementation", path*, symbolName*, view*, limit?, line?, occurrence?, …] | [operation:"references", path*, symbolName*, contextLines?, includeDeclaration?, limit?, line?, …] | [operation:"references", path*, symbolName*, view*, includeDeclaration?, limit?, line?, …] | [operation:"callers", path*, symbolName*, depth?, limit?, line?, occurrence?, …] | [operation:"callees"|"supertypes", path*, symbolName*, depth?, limit?, line?, occurrence?, …] | [operation:"subtypes", path*, symbolName*, depth?, limit?, line?, occurrence?, …] | [operation:"hover", path*, symbolName*, limit?, line?, occurrence?, workspaceRoot?] | [operation:"documentSymbols"|"diagnostic", path*, limit?, workspaceRoot?] | [operation:"workspaceSymbol", path*, symbolFuzzy*, limit?, workspaceRoot?] | [operation:"workspaceSymbol", symbolFuzzy*, workspaceRoot*, limit?]
tools.help:
Examples:
  octocode lspSearch '{"queries":[{"path":"src/index.ts","symbolName":"run","line":10}]}'
  octocode lspSearch '{"queries":[{"path":"src/index.ts","symbolName":"run","line":10,"view":"files"}]}'
  octocode lspSearch '{"queries":[{"operation":"references","path":"src/index.ts","symbolName":"run","line":10}]}'
  octocode lspSearch '{
    "queries": [{"operation":"references","path":"src/index.ts","symbolName":"run","line":10,"view":"files","testCode":"exclude"}]
  }'
  octocode lspSearch '{"queries":[{"operation":"callers","path":"src/index.ts","symbolName":"run","line":10}]}'
  octocode lspSearch '{"queries":[{"operation":"callees","path":"src/index.ts","symbolName":"run","line":10}]}'
  octocode lspSearch '{"queries":[{"operation":"subtypes","path":"src/index.ts","symbolName":"Runner","line":10}]}'
  octocode lspSearch '{"queries":[{"operation":"hover","path":"src/index.ts","symbolName":"run","line":10}]}'
  octocode lspSearch '{"queries":[{"path":"src/index.ts","operation":"documentSymbols"}]}'
  octocode lspSearch '{"queries":[{"operation":"workspaceSymbol","path":"src/index.ts","symbolFuzzy":"run"}]}'
  octocode lspSearch '{"queries":[{"operation":"workspaceSymbol","workspaceRoot":".","symbolFuzzy":"run"}]}'

Input: {"queries":[…]} for fresh calls, optionally with "responseChars" (the size of each response page; the rest pages, nothing dropped; local walk rows still page at the automatic window); copy {"cursor":"…"} from a continuation.
Up to 5 queries per call.

Required fields, by operation:
  definition, typeDefinition, implementation              path, symbolName
  definition, typeDefinition, implementation (with view)  path, symbolName, view
  references                                              path, symbolName, operation
  references (with view)                                  path, symbolName, operation, view
  callers                                                 path, symbolName, operation
  callees, supertypes                                     path, symbolName, operation
  subtypes                                                path, symbolName, operation
  hover                                                   path, symbolName, operation
  documentSymbols, diagnostic                             path, operation
  workspaceSymbol                                         operation, symbolFuzzy, path
  workspaceSymbol                                         workspaceRoot, operation, symbolFuzzy

Each form's example: octocode schema lspSearch --view variants

Fields: octocode schema lspSearch

output.warnings: Notes for the whole response; each applies to every row.
output.oversized: This response holds an indivisible value longer than responseChars; nothing is cut. Fixed envelope parts, repeated context and next may exceed the target without this flag. Per-call metadata (rateLimit, clientWaits, observedAt) and rejected queries are not counted.
output.next: Branches of this row: recover it, read another section or widen its coverage; run each unchanged. The rest of the row itself rides the reply's top-level next. Only this field, never hints, may satisfy isPartial.
output.next.nextPage: The next page of this row's walk; the runtime serves it as the reply's top-level next, one call for every unfinished row.
output.next.nextImporterWindow: Verifies the next window of candidate importer files (the TS/JS importer scan); offered on each of this window's location pages, so every candidate is verified in exactly one window.
output.next.continueWalk: Resumes a hierarchy walk that stopped at its node cap or fan-out, re-anchored on a parent whose children were dropped; one per such parent (continueWalk, continueWalk2, …).
output.next.nextCandidatePage: Judges the units this page left unjudged (its budget ran out or the provider could not answer); billed.
output.next.readDeclaration: Reads the rest of a declaration body this row clipped (localFetch); one per clipped body (readDeclaration, readDeclaration2, …).
output.next.sourceDefinition: Reads the source declaration a definition in a package's build output (a tsconfig outDir .d.ts) was compiled from, mapped through that tsconfig's rootDir and outDir.
output.next.retry: The same call again after a transient failure; retryable says whether it can succeed.
output.next.restart: The request again from its first page, without its cursor: the source changed, so nothing the earlier pages showed remains valid.
output.replayed: Present (true) only on a page read back from saved output, without acquisition or inference; any usage in the output is historical.
output.commitSha: The commit checked out (git HEAD) in the one work tree, inside the allowed roots, that holds every path of the row: cite it with those paths. Absent: the paths span work trees or lie in none. Files can hold uncommitted edits.
output.errorCode: Machine code of the failure; errorClass says what to do next.
output.errorClass: The recovery the failure allows; the instructions name each class.
output.httpStatus: The provider's HTTP status, only when errorCode does not name it (a 5xx under server, an unmapped status under httpStatus, a status the provider read differently); a 401, 403, 404, 429 or 451 is errorCode alone.
output.retryable: On a transient row: whether a retry can succeed.
output.ssoUrl: GitHub SAML SSO authorization URL (x-github-sso) for a 403 whose token must be authorized for the org; open it, then retry.
output.clientWaits: Waits this row spent on the client before its provider requests, by kind: latency the provider did not cause.
output.observedAt: ISO time a reused saved answer was observed, when the origin's own lifetime does not vouch for it (a disclosed reuse window, or a stale answer during a rate limit): the origin was not asked again, so later changes are not shown. An answer within the origin's max-age is served as current, without observedAt.
output.redacted: Present (true) only when secret-shaped text in this row became [REDACTED-…] placeholders; the rest is verbatim.
output.rateLimit: The provider's rate limit behind a failure: when a retry can run.
output.rateLimit.resource: The provider's limit bucket, e.g. core or search.
output.hints: Hints every empty or failed result row of this response states; those rows omit them. Optional guidance for empty results or errors; evidence and coverage disclosures go in warnings, executable follow-ups in objects. Related calls never complete a partial result.
output.pagination: Where this window sits, or an exact count; a reply that carries a top-level next reads on. For completeness see partialReasons and terminalLimit.
output.pagination.unit: What offset, length and total count, stated only for text windows: lines (localSearch hit rows: a matched line, or each hit window of a long line; a body's lines), bytes or chars. Absent for row lists: total counts the rows of the operation (commits, pullRequests, matches, tree entries) and offset is the first row of the page.
output.pagination.offset: Where this page starts in unit, from 0. A bytes window counts the source text as served, never the N\t gutters: decoded (a BOM dropped, UTF-16 as UTF-8), each redaction placeholder as the bytes it shows, so it can differ from the file's bytes.
output.pagination.length: How many units this page holds, stated with a text window's unit; absent for row lists, where the rows listed are the page.
output.pagination.total: Exact size of the whole list or body in unit; absent when unknown or only a floor. A read counts what it selects (its ranges, matches or transformed view), not the file: data.totalLines counts the file, and a lines window states total only when it differs.
output.pagination.oversized: A bytes or chars window shows an indivisible redaction marker whole: its text is wider than length, cut short of the marker, or empty when the marker belongs to the next window. Offsets stay nominal; walking on still reads every unit once.
output.isPartial: True when this row misses part of the requested scope for a reason pagination does not state; more pages show as the reply's top-level next, not as isPartial. Absent when partialReasons states it. Inspect next, partialReasons, warnings and terminalLimit.
output.terminalLimit: True when a provider or runtime limit leaves part of the requested scope unreachable by any call; report that scope. A next call still reads the rest, so keep walking.
output.partialReasons: Machine-readable reasons this row has incomplete coverage.
output.coverage: complete covers the stated scope; partial leaves evidence unread, so absence is unproven; error: nothing was judged. reason explains a gap; next.* may offer drill-downs even when complete. A page is partial when isPartial is true or partialReasons is present; it states that once.
output.coverage.state: Absent when partial and stated by isPartial or partialReasons.
output.coverage.textOnlyFiles: Files under the search scope, within the declaration's reach, that spell the name as a word in a way that could answer the question but are not in the answer; 0 clears file-level partial reasons.
output.coverage.outOfReachFiles: Files the text check read that spell the name outside the declaration's reach (its visibility, its crate, or a local binding's scope): not missed sites, not partial.
output.coverage.unreadOutOfReach: Files of the scope outside the declaration's reach (a Rust module, crate or local binding) that the text check did not read: they cannot reference it, so they are not missed sites and the row is not partial. Counted apart from outOfReachFiles.
output.coverage.importerScan: The TS/JS importer scan that adds files the server did not report, stated when it did not end clean: capped, later importer windows remain (next.nextImporterWindow); failed, cross-file results unverified. Absent: every candidate verified, or no scan ran.
output.coverage.verifiedImporterFiles: Importer files the scan verified beyond the server's answer; present only above 0 (absent: it added none, not that nothing was verified).
output.coverage.tooLargeFiles: Importer candidates that spell the name but are larger than a language server is sent (a vendored bundle): counted instead of verified, not a failed scan; the related localSearch reads them.
output.coverage.packageImporters: TS/JS importer files that bind the name through the anchor package's build output (its tsconfig outDir .d.ts) that the scan could not map back to this source declaration: unverified, so the row is partial (importUnresolved); the related localSearch reads them.
output.coverage.cfgGatedFiles: Rust files missing from the answer that use the name in code under a cfg gate the analyzed configuration leaves out (partialReasons cfgGatedFiles).
output.coverage.importerScanRoot: The request's workspaceRoot bounded the scan below the repository: importers outside it went unscanned.
output.root: Stated once when the row's evidence lies outside the workspace (a clone, a materialized tree, another allowed root): the absolute root every path of the row is named from; root + "/" + path names the file, while the row's calls keep absolute paths. Absent: paths are workspace-relative.
output.sourceEvidence: Exact descriptor closure for this response fragment's origins. Each origin and descriptor stays atomic; projection limits fail explicitly.
output.sourceEvidence.snapshots[]: Original file bytes. latin1 is 8-bit text read one character per byte; lossy is UTF-8 with stray bytes, each run read as U+FFFD. Identity commits to the authorized source occurrence and raw digest, not the displayed path alone.
output.sourceEvidence.representations[]: UTF-8 parser representation. sourceIds is its unique raw-source closure, empty for decoded-only input. Identity includes derivation, not just content.
output.sourceEvidence.representations[].produce: Registered producer identity and implementation version.
output.sourceEvidence.units[]: Ordered analyzed regions in the identified representation. Empty input uses [0,0]; excluded gaps are not analyzed source.
output.sourceEvidence.units[].adapter: Registered producer identity and implementation version.
output.sourceEvidence.units[].regions[]: Half-open byte range. Its owning field identifies the representation; endpoints must be ordered.
output.testCodeExcluded: What testCode left out: test code, or production code under "only".
output.testCodeExcluded.files: Files left out (listings: entries left out). A file a module root mounts as test code by #[path] is left out unread; one another module mounts counts once a hit or listing reaches it.
output.testCodeExcluded.lines: Hit lines left out inside searched files.
output.path: The queried file or directory, named as a row path (from root when stated).
output.lsp.level: Which engine answered: ide the editor's providers through the Octocode extension; server a language server Octocode started; syntax tree-sitter facts matched by name (unverified); text no engine, follow the leads.
output.lsp.fellBackFrom: The better engine that did not answer, and why.
output.lsp.ide: The editor whose providers answered at level ide.
output.lsp.source: How a fallback request was answered: heritage or implementation the server through heritage clauses or textDocument/implementation; native-graph-facts a source scan (unverified).
output.lsp.analysisContext: Observed diagnostic and configuration context; neither configuration presence nor no reported errors proves usable compilation or complete indexing.
output.lsp.analysisContext.diagnostics: unavailable: no diagnostics report for the answered document version arrived, so errors are not ruled out; noErrorsReported: the report listed none; errors: errorCount counts them.
output.resolvedSymbol: Present only when the anchor was found elsewhere than requested (another line or file, or a line spelling the name more than once): cite foundAtLine and path.
output.resolvedSymbol.foundAtLine: The line the name was found on; absent when it is line.
output.resolvedSymbol.foundAtCharacter: 1-based column (UTF-16 units) of the name anchored on.
output.resolvedSymbol.occurrencesOnLine: Spellings of the name on the anchored line, when 2+.
output.resolvedSymbol.alternatives: Other readings of the anchor, nearest first: another spelling on the line {occurrence, foundAtCharacter, symbolName?}, or a line a stale line number may have meant {foundAtLine, foundAtCharacter, lineDeviation}. The warning lists every line spelling the name.
output.matchCount: References in this answer (an importer window past the first counts its own rows).
output.matchedFiles: Files holding a hit in this answer.
output.category: Why an answer is empty: noLocations, notCallable (callers or callees on a type, enum or trait: use references or implementation), noHover, noDiagnostics, diagnosticsNotPublished, locationsWithheld, languageServerIndexing, noProject (no project file above the file: not absence).
output.reason: Absent when category says it all.

output.expansionFailures: Every distinct hierarchy-expansion error with its count.

output.shared.data: Facts every result row of this response states alike; those rows omit them. A row reads a field it lacks from its nearest holder, then its data, then here, then the request.
output.shared.data.coverage: complete covers the stated scope; partial leaves evidence unread, so absence is unproven; error: nothing was judged. reason explains a gap; next.* may offer drill-downs even when complete. output.related: Optional fresh calls, each merging the rows' one-query related calls of one tool; run unchanged.
output.error: Why the whole call was rejected.

query.name: lspSearch
query.description:
<when>Resolve definitions, uses, callers or types of a symbol at a line, or by name in the file that declares it.</when>
Example: {"queries":[{"operation":"callers","path":"src/index.ts","symbolName":"run","line":10}]}
A language's first call may wait seconds for its server. Fetched code (clones, ghStructure materialize): no server by default; on errorCode policy use localSearch or astSearch.
Method references and callers can include interface calls. importerScan capped: run next.nextImporterWindow too. Text and importer scans skip gitignored and hidden files.
Not proof of absence: empty with lsp.analysisContext errors; workspaceSymbol; lsp.level syntax or text.

querySchema.description: For symbolName, line, occurrence: never with operation: documentSymbols, diagnostic, workspaceSymbol. For view, contextLines: only with operation: definition, typeDefinition, implementation, references.

limit.description: documentSymbols: top-level declarations, each with its members. Omit: the automatic page window (a default size) per row; limit only shrinks it.

path.description: workspaceSymbol: a file of the project to search (none known: localSearch or structureSearch); a directory or workspaceRoot searches one server-picked project (partial; hint names it). Required except with operation: workspaceSymbol.

symbolName.description: Required with operation: definition, typeDefinition, implementation, references, callers, callees, supertypes, subtypes, hover.

line.description: 1-based line spelling symbolName. Omit: the one declaration of symbolName in path.

occurrence.description: With line: 0-based among identifiers spelled symbolName on it, left to right.

operation.description: workspaceSymbol needs one of: path, workspaceRoot.

contextLines.description: Omit: whole declaration (more: next.readDeclaration); {before:0,after:0}: line only. Only with view: content.

includeDeclaration.description: false: no declaration row. Only with operation: references.

testCode.description: Test files and dirs by convention, plus Rust #[cfg(test)] items. Omit: include. Only with operation: references, callers.

depth.description: Only with operation: callers, callees, supertypes, subtypes.

tools.name: securityCheck
tools.title: Security Check
tools.fields: [operation:"package", ecosystem*, packageName*, preview?, release?, version?, view?] | [operation:"url", url*, preview?, view?] | [operation:"advisory", id*, owner?, preview?, repo?, view?] | [operation:"commit", ref*, owner?, preview?, repo?, view?] | [operation:"repository", owner*, repo*, preview?, view?]
tools.help:
Examples:
  octocode securityCheck '{"queries":[{"operation":"package","ecosystem":"npm","packageName":"lodash","version":"4.17.20"}]}'
  octocode securityCheck '{"queries":[{"operation":"url","url":"https://www.npmjs.com/package/lodash"}]}'
  octocode securityCheck '{"queries":[{"operation":"advisory","id":"GHSA-29mw-wpgm-hmr9"}]}'
  octocode securityCheck '{"queries":[{"operation":"commit","ref":"6879efc2c1596d11a6a6ad296f80063b558d5e0f"}]}'
  octocode securityCheck '{"queries":[{"operation":"repository","owner":"tmcw","repo":"leftpad"}]}'

Input: {"queries":[…]} for fresh calls, optionally with "responseChars" (the size of each response page; the rest pages, nothing dropped; local walk rows still page at the automatic window); copy {"cursor":"…"} from a continuation.
Up to 5 queries per call.

Required fields, by operation:
  package     operation, ecosystem, packageName
  url         operation, url
  advisory    operation, id
  commit      operation, ref
  repository  operation, owner, repo

Each form's example: octocode schema securityCheck --view variants

Fields: octocode schema securityCheck

output.warnings: Notes for the whole response; each applies to every row.
output.oversized: This response holds an indivisible value longer than responseChars; nothing is cut. Fixed envelope parts, repeated context and next may exceed the target without this flag. Per-call metadata (rateLimit, clientWaits, observedAt) and rejected queries are not counted.
output.next: Branches of this row: recover it, read another section or widen its coverage; run each unchanged. The rest of the row itself rides the reply's top-level next. Only this field, never hints, may satisfy isPartial.
output.next.nextPage: The next page of this row's walk; the runtime serves it as the reply's top-level next, one call for every unfinished row.
output.next.repair: The corrected call for this row's error (for example the last page this page size reaches); run it unchanged.
output.next.retry: The same call again after a transient failure; retryable says whether it can succeed.
output.next.restart: The request again from its first page, without its cursor: the source changed, so nothing the earlier pages showed remains valid.
output.replayed: Present (true) only on a page read back from saved output, without acquisition or inference; any usage in the output is historical.
output.commitSha: The resolved source commit for this result.
output.errorCode: Machine code of the failure; errorClass says what to do next.
output.errorClass: The recovery the failure allows; the instructions name each class.
output.httpStatus: The provider's HTTP status, only when errorCode does not name it (a 5xx under server, an unmapped status under httpStatus, a status the provider read differently); a 401, 403, 404, 429 or 451 is errorCode alone.
output.retryable: On a transient row: whether a retry can succeed.
output.ssoUrl: GitHub SAML SSO authorization URL (x-github-sso) for a 403 whose token must be authorized for the org; open it, then retry.
output.clientWaits: Waits this row spent on the client before its provider requests, by kind: latency the provider did not cause.
output.observedAt: ISO time a reused saved answer was observed, when the origin's own lifetime does not vouch for it (a disclosed reuse window, or a stale answer during a rate limit): the origin was not asked again, so later changes are not shown. An answer within the origin's max-age is served as current, without observedAt.
output.redacted: Present (true) only when secret-shaped text in this row became [REDACTED-…] placeholders; the rest is verbatim.
output.rateLimit: The provider's rate limit behind a failure: when a retry can run.
output.rateLimit.resource: The provider's limit bucket, e.g. core or search.
output.hints: Hints every empty or failed result row of this response states; those rows omit them. Optional guidance for empty results or errors; evidence and coverage disclosures go in warnings, executable follow-ups in objects. Related calls never complete a partial result.
output.pagination: Where this window sits, or an exact count; a reply that carries a top-level next reads on. For completeness see partialReasons and terminalLimit.
output.pagination.unit: What offset, length and total count, stated only for text windows: lines (localSearch hit rows: a matched line, or each hit window of a long line; a body's lines), bytes or chars. Absent for row lists: total counts the rows of the operation (commits, pullRequests, matches, tree entries) and offset is the first row of the page.
output.pagination.offset: Where this page starts in unit, from 0. A bytes window counts the source text as served, never the N\t gutters: decoded (a BOM dropped, UTF-16 as UTF-8), each redaction placeholder as the bytes it shows, so it can differ from the file's bytes.
output.pagination.length: How many units this page holds, stated with a text window's unit; absent for row lists, where the rows listed are the page.
output.pagination.total: Exact size of the whole list or body in unit; absent when unknown or only a floor. A read counts what it selects (its ranges, matches or transformed view), not the file: data.totalLines counts the file, and a lines window states total only when it differs.
output.pagination.oversized: A bytes or chars window shows an indivisible redaction marker whole: its text is wider than length, cut short of the marker, or empty when the marker belongs to the next window. Offsets stay nominal; walking on still reads every unit once.
output.isPartial: True when this row misses part of the requested scope for a reason pagination does not state; more pages show as the reply's top-level next, not as isPartial. Absent when partialReasons states it. Inspect next, partialReasons, warnings and terminalLimit.
output.terminalLimit: True when a provider or runtime limit leaves part of the requested scope unreachable by any call; report that scope. A next call still reads the rest, so keep walking.
output.partialReasons: Machine-readable reasons this row has incomplete coverage.
output.coverage: complete covers the stated scope; partial leaves evidence unread, so absence is unproven; error: nothing was judged. reason explains a gap; next.* may offer drill-downs even when complete. A page is partial when isPartial is true or partialReasons is present; it states that once.
output.coverage.state: Absent when partial and stated by isPartial or partialReasons.
output.preview: Local egress preview. No provider request or classification charge occurred.
output.preview.destinations[].origin: Destination origin without credentials or query parameters.
output.preview.destinations[].when: Condition under which the live request contacts this destination.
output.preview.destinations[].sends: Coordinates or data categories the destination would receive.
output.preview.selection: Sanitized classification selection. Remote source references represent inputs still to be fetched.
output.preview.redaction: How selected text and image pixels are handled.
output.answer: The result in one sentence of typed values, with no text from a source: the target, whether it is affected, what to upgrade to, which CVEs. view summary keeps only the clauses no field states (an advisory's ranges, why a target has no verdict), and omits answer when none is left.
output.affected: true: OSV matched this target. false: none known to OSV at this version, which proves only that. Absent: not known, as for a version not evaluated or an empty commit.
output.upgradeTo: The lowest fixed version clearing every listed advisory, compared in the registry's version order (a prerelease fix counts): a stable release unless the deciding fix is a prerelease with no stable release published above it, which upgradeNote then says. Checked with OSV at that version, and published on the registry, not yanked.
output.advisoryCount: view summary: advisories counted for the target, withdrawn ones left out. Absent: not checked, or the walk has not ended.
output.highestSeverity: view summary: the most severe label among the counted advisories, as their databases word it. An advisory whose database states no word ranks by the qualitative rating of its CVSS base score (v3.x: none, low, medium, high, critical; v2: low, medium, high), its published score or else one computed from its v3.x or v2 vector for this ranking only, and that rating is the label. cvss[].score stays as published. Absent: none states a word or a v3.x or v2 vector.
output.unfixedInMajorCount: view summary: counted advisories no release of version's own major is listed as fixing, so upgradeTo is in a later major. Absent: none.
output.link: Present only when it is not https://osv.dev/vulnerability/<id> of the first listed advisory; otherwise open that page.
output.upgradeNote: Why no upgrade is named, or what OSV lists at upgradeTo besides. View summary: only with no upgradeTo, or when upgradeTo is a prerelease.
output.packageName: The public registry's name for the package, as sent to OSV.
output.version: The exact version the registry confirmed; every advisory is OSV's match for it.
output.registryConfirmed: The public registry did not confirm the name (no registry reader for this ecosystem, or the registry no longer lists it): OSV matched the text sent, and a misspelled name reads as none known.
output.latestVersion: The registry's latest stable version: view details states it, view summary when outdated and different from upgradeTo (which then is the latest). Absent there: the registry read failed or has no such notion.
output.latestPublishedAt: When latestVersion was published, as YYYY-MM-DD.
output.currentPublishedAt: When version was published, as YYYY-MM-DD.
output.outdated: A newer release exists, published after version; false when version equals latestVersion. View summary states only false: a newer release is the one named by latestVersion or upgradeTo. Absent: not known; false is not safe.
output.upgradeKind: What moving to latestVersion changes, compared as plain dotted numbers; unknown otherwise, never guessed.
output.cautions: Signals to review before relying on this target, each with its raw values. lowTraction alone is a note. Absent: none fired, or trust was not evaluated: see repository and sources.
output.cautions[].level: review: look before relying on it. note: context only.
output.cautions[].rule: lowTraction: The repository has fewer than 100 stars. unmaintained: No push to the repository for more than 365 days. archived: The repository is archived: read-only, no fixes will land. deprecated: The registry marks this version or package deprecated. yanked: The registry yanked or retracted this version. repositoryMissing: The repository the registry names does not exist. repositoryMoved: The repository the registry names moved or was renamed. noSourceRepo: The registry names no source repository; trust was not evaluated. lookalikeName: Another name one edit away (this name with a character dropped, two adjacent characters swapped, or a separator - _ . added, dropped or changed) has at least 1000 times its downloads on the registry: a possible typosquat or misspelling. Checked only for unscoped npm names (last-week downloads) and crates.io (90-day downloads). commitNotInRepository: GitHub has no such commit in the repository. onlyInForkNetwork: The commit resolves through the repository but is the head of no branch, the tip of no tag, in no pull request and in the history of no branch or tag: it may live only in a fork. malware: A source reports malicious code in this package: GitHub's advisory database classes a record as malware, or OSV lists a malicious-packages report (MAL-); on a package row, at the version asked. why names each.
output.cautions[].basis: reported: a source states it. heuristic: a threshold in policy inferred it.
output.cautions[].why: The raw values, the threshold and today's date, as typed facts.
output.repository: The source repository GitHub described: package rows, commit with repo, and the repository operation. Absent: none named or GitHub unread: see sources.
output.repository.url: The page when it is not github.com/owner/repo.
output.repository.pushedAt: Last push to any branch, as YYYY-MM-DD; never updated_at, which an archive or a star can move.
output.repository.provenance: How the package's link to this repository is established. claimed: the registry says so. verified: a signed attestation or a matching tag proves it. A claimed repository can add a caution, never clear one.
output.repository.namedBy: The latest release names this repository; the version's own is not on GitHub (cautions name both).
output.repository.readOn: The day these facts were read.
output.versionListed: The registry does not list the requested version (never published, yanked or removed); OSV's ranges were matched at it: affected and the advisories are OSV's match. Check the spelling; do not install it.
output.nearestVersions: With versionListed false: the versions the registry does list nearest the requested one, none yanked and none checked here: run this check on one before moving to it.
output.versionEvaluated: The requested version is not on the public registry, so OSV was asked about the package only: read each advisory's affected ranges. Absent with versionListed: OSV was asked at the version.
output.sources: Each source asked; view summary lists only one that failed, stopped early or does not cover the target. A failed source leaves the row partial (sourceFailed), never clean; the row keeps what the others answered. A resumed page whose OSV read fails is an error.
output.sources[].status: found: it holds advisories for the target. noneKnown: a finished walk found none, which proves only that source; GitHub describing a target it holds none for is noneKnown, its description in repository or facts. partial: it stopped early; the reply's next reads on. failed: it was asked and did not answer, never clean. unavailable: not asked, for want of a token or quota. notCovered: it does not cover this target, as a repository off GitHub. Statuses are independent per source: github noneKnown beside osv found is consistent.
output.sources[].facts: What this source stated of the target.
output.sources[].facts.exists: GitHub has this commit in the repository.
output.sources[].facts.signature: GitHub's verification of the commit; unverified is a note, not a finding.
output.sources[].facts.heads: Branches whose head is this commit; absent: not read.
output.sources[].facts.pulls: Pull requests that contain this commit; absent: not read.
output.sources[].facts.onDefaultBranch: The default branch's history holds this commit; absent: not read.
output.sources[].facts.inBranch: Branches whose history holds this commit, read only when no head, pull request, tag or default branch holds it; complete only when inRefsComplete is true.
output.sources[].facts.inTag: Tags that point at this commit; when none does and nothing else holds it, the tags whose history holds it, complete only when inRefsComplete is true. Absent: not read.
output.sources[].facts.inRefsComplete: With inBranch or inTag from history: true when every branch and tag was compared; false when the walk ended at the page that found a holder or a comparison failed, so other refs may hold it too.
output.sources[].facts.repositoryAdvisories: Ids of the repository's published advisories that OSV does not list for this commit or version (a package row: those naming the package whose own range does not exclude the version): the repository's word, not counted in answer; the repository operation reads each with its ranges. Partial when why names an advisory stop.
output.sources[].facts.globalAdvisories: Ids of advisories GitHub matches to this version and OSV does not list (withdrawn ones excluded): GitHub's word, not counted in answer; the advisory operation reads each.
output.sources[].errorCode: Why failed or unavailable: the source's own refusal, such as a rate limit.
output.sources[].why: What this source left unread and why, with what to do about it (retry later, sign in). A GitHub refusal the rows share, such as a rate limit with its reset time and the sign-in that raises the quota, is stated once in warnings; each entry keeps its errorCode.
output.sources[].anonymous: GitHub was read without a token: public data only, under the anonymous rate limit, so a private repository or advisory reads as missing. Sign in to read them.
output.advisories: view details: one row per source record, once every source finished. Records sharing an id remain separate, told apart by database; only textSameAs refers to another record. An omitted collection within a record means no selected items stated there, without distinguishing an absent upstream field from an empty array. view summary: each advisory advisoryCount counts, once, most severe first, as what decides an upgrade (id, cves, severity or cvss, fixedIn; withdrawn ones are left out); the advisory operation lists one row per advisory (id, aliases, CVEs, severity, summary, fixedIn, link); its view details reads one whole, with references. view details omits a link equal to https://osv.dev/vulnerability/ plus the id. []: a finished check found none known to OSV, a floor rather than proof. Absent: not checked.
output.advisories[].cves: Omitted when it would only repeat the row's own id.
output.advisories[].link: The provider's advisory page. Absent when `source` is the same address.
output.advisories[].database: The database this copy comes from; the same advisory id can appear once per database.
output.advisories[].source: One source-record location reported by the provider; affected metadata retains each entry's source locations and attribution.
output.advisories[].githubType: GitHub's class of the record: unreviewed, GitHub has not checked it; malware, the package itself is malicious. Absent: not GitHub's database, or it states none.
output.advisories[].publisher: The GitHub account that published a repository advisory.
output.advisories[].credits: Who the source credits, with GitHub's credit type.
output.advisories[].severity: The database's own label, lowercased; absent when it gave none.
output.advisories[].cvss: CVSS as each source published it.
output.advisories[].cvss[].score: The base score the source publishes with the vector, as GitHub does; absent: it gives the vector only, as OSV does. Never computed here.
output.advisories[].epss: GitHub's EPSS for the advisory; absent: GitHub states none, or its record was not read.
output.advisories[].epss.percentage: Probability of exploitation in the next 30 days.
output.advisories[].epss.percentile: Share of scored CVEs with this probability or less.
output.advisories[].textSameAs: Link of an earlier record of this id holding the summary and details omitted here as equal, line endings aside.
output.advisories[].fixedIn: Fix versions only. A package row with a version lists the one fix for that version's line; the advisory read lists every fixed version, one per affected range in OSV order, and none when the advisory names several packages; upgradeTo is the one that clears the queried version. Omitted when this record's own affected ranges already state every selected fix, or when none is stated; never proof of no fix. A version is safe only outside every affected range.
output.advisories[].withdrawn: When the advisory was withdrawn: retracted, not a finding. An advisory's records (aliases) count as withdrawn only when every record is.
output.advisories[].alsoAffects: Other packages this record names; link holds their ranges.
output.advisories[].disputedBy: Aliases another database keeps for this package that OSV does not list at this version: the databases disagree. The row still counts it, as OSV lists it; read each record's ranges.
output.advisories[].affected: The selected affected entries with the package identity each source states. A package query selects its own entries; an advisory query includes every entry.
output.advisories[].affected[].ecosystem: The package ecosystem as the ecosystem input spells it, with any distribution release suffix.
output.advisories[].affected[].purl: Package URL exactly as the source states it, including any version, qualifiers or subpath. Absent when the source states none.
output.advisories[].affected[].ecosystemSpecifi: This entry's ecosystem-specific metadata, including source keys as supplied.
output.advisories[].affected[].databaseSpecific: This entry's database-specific metadata, including source keys and range statements as supplied. Its source is omitted when it equals the record's source.
output.advisories[].references: This provider's selected references, preserving their order and types. Omitted: no selected items stated in this record. Never inherited from another record.
output.moduleOnly: Go module advisories whose records name other packages of this module in their imports, not this one; not counted in answer or advisories.
output.moduleOnly.advisories[].cves: Omitted when it would only repeat the row's own id.
output.moduleOnly.advisories[].link: The provider's advisory page. Absent when `source` is the same address.
output.moduleOnly.advisories[].database: The database this copy comes from; the same advisory id can appear once per database.
output.moduleOnly.advisories[].source: One source-record location reported by the provider; affected metadata retains each entry's source locations and attribution.
output.moduleOnly.advisories[].githubType: GitHub's class of the record: unreviewed, GitHub has not checked it; malware, the package itself is malicious. Absent: not GitHub's database, or it states none.
output.moduleOnly.advisories[].publisher: The GitHub account that published a repository advisory.
output.moduleOnly.advisories[].credits: Who the source credits, with GitHub's credit type.
output.moduleOnly.advisories[].severity: The database's own label, lowercased; absent when it gave none.
output.moduleOnly.advisories[].cvss: CVSS as each source published it.
output.moduleOnly.advisories[].cvss[].score: The base score the source publishes with the vector, as GitHub does; absent: it gives the vector only, as OSV does. Never computed here.
output.moduleOnly.advisories[].epss: GitHub's EPSS for the advisory; absent: GitHub states none, or its record was not read.
output.moduleOnly.advisories[].epss.percentage: Probability of exploitation in the next 30 days.
output.moduleOnly.advisories[].epss.percentile: Share of scored CVEs with this probability or less.
output.moduleOnly.advisories[].textSameAs: Link of an earlier record of this id holding the summary and details omitted here as equal, line endings aside.
output.moduleOnly.advisories[].fixedIn: Fix versions only. A package row with a version lists the one fix for that version's line; the advisory read lists every fixed version, one per affected range in OSV order, and none when the advisory names several packages; upgradeTo is the one that clears the queried version. Omitted when this record's own affected ranges already state every selected fix, or when none is stated; never proof of no fix. A version is safe only outside every affected range.
output.moduleOnly.advisories[].withdrawn: When the advisory was withdrawn: retracted, not a finding. An advisory's records (aliases) count as withdrawn only when every record is.
output.moduleOnly.advisories[].alsoAffects: Other packages this record names; link holds their ranges.
output.moduleOnly.advisories[].disputedBy: Aliases another database keeps for this package that OSV does not list at this version: the databases disagree. The row still counts it, as OSV lists it; read each record's ranges.
output.moduleOnly.advisories[].affected: The selected affected entries with the package identity each source states. A package query selects its own entries; an advisory query includes every entry.
output.moduleOnly.advisories[].affected[].ecosy: The package ecosystem as the ecosystem input spells it, with any distribution release suffix.
output.moduleOnly.advisories[].affected[].purl: Package URL exactly as the source states it, including any version, qualifiers or subpath. Absent when the source states none.
output.moduleOnly.advisories[].affected[].ecosy: This entry's ecosystem-specific metadata, including source keys as supplied.
output.moduleOnly.advisories[].affected[].datab: This entry's database-specific metadata, including source keys and range statements as supplied. Its source is omitted when it equals the record's source.
output.moduleOnly.advisories[].references: This provider's selected references, preserving their order and types. Omitted: no selected items stated in this record. Never inherited from another record.
output.results[].status: Absent: evidence. empty: nothing in the asked scope matched; the row's other facts still hold. error: errorCode says why. outOfRange: a page past the end; pagination.total states the size (next.restart).
output.results[].rowPart: This row spans replies; concatenate its parts in order.
output.results[].rowPart.continues: The innermost array element this part continues; pointer indexes are the joined row's, and each element on the pointer path also continues.
output.results[].rowPart.continues.array: JSON pointer of the array this part resumes.
output.results[].rowPart.text: JSON pointer, in the joined row's indexes, of the string this part continues: append this part's value there to the previous part's.
output.shared.data: Facts every result row of this response states alike; those rows omit them. A row reads a field it lacks from its nearest holder, then its data, then here, then the request.
output.shared.data.coverage: complete covers the stated scope; partial leaves evidence unread, so absence is unproven; error: nothing was judged. reason explains a gap; next.* may offer drill-downs even when complete. A page is partial when isPartial is true or partialReasons is present; it states that once.
output.related: Optional fresh calls, each merging the rows' one-query related calls of one tool; run unchanged.
output.error: Why the whole call was rejected.

query.name: securityCheck
query.description:
<when>Check a dependency's known advisories and fixes before use: package coordinates, registry URL or purl, advisory id, commit hash or GitHub repo.</when>
Example: {"queries":[{"operation":"package","ecosystem":"npm","packageName":"lodash","version":"4.17.20"}]}
OSV receives every name, version (even registry misses) and commit hash: never a private commit.
An advisory's text, ranges, references (fix commits, PRs): advisory, view details. affected false: none known, not safe.

querySchema.description: For ecosystem, packageName: required only with operation: package. For version, release: only with operation: package. For owner, repo: never with operation: package, url. For owner, repo: required with operation: repository.

preview.description: Show destinations and selected data offline.

packageName.description: maven: group:artifact. go: module/package path. SwiftURL, GitHub Actions: repo path. Distros: source package.

version.description: npm, pypi, crates: a range or tag checks only its newest match. Omit: registry's latest stable, else every version.

release.description: Distros only: 12, 22.04:LTS, v3.18; not Wolfi, Chainguard. Omit: Debian, Ubuntu count all releases' advisories; others go unevaluated.

view.description: summary: verdict, upgradeTo, cautions, each counted advisory's id, CVEs, severity, fixedIn. details: every database's whole record (text, ranges, references), paged; repo and source facts.

url.description: Registry page, purl, or GitHub advisory, repo or commit URL; deb/apk/rpm purl distro= is the release. Required only with operation: url.

id.description: OSV id: CVE-, GHSA-, GO-, PYSEC-, RUSTSEC-, DSA-, MAL-, OSV-; with owner and repo, also that repo's GHSA advisories. Required only with operation: advisory.

ref.description: Full SHA; with owner and repo, GitHub also checks it there. Required only with operation: commit.
